data.narrative:
Kairos Power is a late-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $500M+ to date. The valuation universe for comparable analysis includes 3 public peers (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private nuclear companies, notably Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Given the sector's limited comparable depth, a single quantitative method proved applicable. Stage-Progression analysis uses $500M in total raised as a proxy base valuation, applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of Late Stage advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $600M. A Peer-Median approach was not viable due to insufficient same-stage or similar-tier comparables within the narrow nuclear energy sector—only one adjacent-stage peer met filter criteria against a minimum threshold of three datapoints, making cross-peer multiples unreliable.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $510M to $690M, with a midpoint of $600M. This range reflects stage-appropriate mark-ups from historical capital deployment, absent direct peer trading multiples. Key uncertainties include the absence of recent late-stage nuclear private transactions, regulatory pathway risk, and technology validation milestones not captured in this analysis. The single-method foundation limits confidence; a second market-based anchor would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
